parsedVerdict.reasoning: The class OrderRepository is a concrete in-memory storage implementation, not a domain abstraction. It keeps its own backing store (`private orders: Map<string, Order>`) and handles saving, lookup and scanning of stored records in `save`, `getById`, `getByState` and `getAll`. That is persistence work, which belongs to an infrastructure-kind layer. A domain layer would normally declare only a repository contract (an interface or port) and leave the implementation to infrastructure. The graph shows that application use cases inject this concrete class directly, so the domain file is the storage mechanism. The in-memory query filtering in getByState is also a storage/query concern rather than a business rule.

violations.message: Class OrderRepository implements concrete persistence (a Map backing store, plus save, getById, getByState and getAll over that store) inside the domain layer. This responsibility belongs to the infrastructure layer kind. The domain should only declare a repository interface.
